claims.explanation: Teniposide is a topoisomerase II poison that traps TOP2A/TOP2B-DNA cleavage complexes, so sensitivity should track with high TOP2A expression and proliferative capacity, while efflux pumps and p53-mediated apoptosis defects blunt killing. The resistant lines are enriched for low TOP2A/neuronal or slow-cycling phenotypes and for drug-efflux or apoptosis-escape features, whereas sensitive lines carry proliferative, DNA-damage-response and oncogene-driven contexts that increase topoisomerase II dependence.

features.basis: teniposide poisons TOP2A; higher target enzyme levels increase cleavage-complex formation
teniposide also targets TOP2B and stimulates TOP2B-mediated DNA cleavage
P-glycoprotein efflux reduces intracellular epipodophyllotoxin and confers resistance
MRP3 transports epipodophyllotoxins and confers low-level teniposide resistance
loss of p53-mediated apoptosis after DNA damage reduces teniposide cytotoxicity
cell-cycle checkpoint loss increases reliance on TOP2-dependent replication and DNA damage
MAPK-driven proliferation raises TOP2A dependence and DNA-damage sensitivity
oncogenic KRAS increases proliferation and topoisomerase II dependence
PI3K pathway activation supports proliferation and DNA-damage sensitivity
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT proliferation and DNA-damage response
SWI/SNF loss alters chromatin and reduces topoisomerase II poison efficacy
ARID1A loss is enriched in least-affected lines and may reduce drug-induced chromatin damage
